date: September 22, 2026 | Target validation before further calibration
summary: The frozen 13-row target/weight system was used consistently. Saved empirical receipts reproduce the measured values; 2.1 is an author normalization and 0.88% is an inherited external restriction. This is not a fresh raw-data replication.

The data-model mapping is not fully closed. Prioritize population/geography, the first-birth rooms estimand and its model counterpart, resident-child groups, and wealth/income concepts. Existing room caps and fractional age masks work in the actual scored code.
No targets or weights have been changed and no overnight utility-comparison jobs have been submitted. A longer fit should follow an explicitly frozen measurement contract.

rows.label: Initial fertility normalization
rows.data: Author-imposed stationary model normalization, not an empirical estimate.
rows.model: The existing normalization solves for the fertility utility scale; no weight in the twelve-row objective.
rows.assessment: Keep its role explicit. Do not interpret 2.1 as a directly measured period birth rate or equate it with every cohort fertility measure.

rows.weight_rationale: CPS official annual generalized-variance approximations pooled with fixed observed weights and correlation-one working convention; not design-exact pooled SE
rows.label: Childless women, ages 40-44
rows.data: June CPS 2004/2006, women 40-44, valid children-ever-born and positive fertility-supplement weight; weighted share with zero children. Saved source estimate reproduced.
rows.model: Uniform birth-time interpolation across four-year age cells, with fractional overlap at 40-44; uses the model household reproductive-member mass.
rows.assessment: Age mapper is implemented. Female population and empirical/model age composition need an explicit common interpretation.

rows.weight_rationale: CPS official annual generalized-variance approximations pooled with fixed observed weights and correlation-one working convention; not design-exact pooled SE
rows.label: Exactly one child among mothers
rows.data: Same CPS sample; weighted share with exactly one child conditional on ever having a child.
rows.model: Exactly-one-child stock divided by the stock of mothers, using the same age projection.
rows.assessment: This is not a second-birth hazard. Reconcile population mapping alongside childlessness; no unavailable-mapper claim.

rows.weight_rationale: 2003–2006 annual temporal SD: chosen typical-year discrepancy scale for approximate stationary target; not sampling SE
rows.label: Mean first-birth age
rows.data: NCHS first-birth counts 2003-2006. Ages are mapped to the model midpoint classes; tails below 18 and above 45 are absorbed into boundary groups. Saved estimate reproduced.
rows.model: First-birth flow weighted mean of model age-cell midpoints in the stationary economy.
rows.assessment: Same grouped-age calculation is available. Stationary versus dated period, population/residence scope and boundary support remain explicit assumptions.

rows.weight_rationale: 2003–2006 annual temporal SD: chosen typical-year discrepancy scale for approximate stationary target; not sampling SE
rows.label: First births at age 30 or above
rows.data: Share of pooled first births at exact maternal age 30 or above, among the saved age 12-49 counts.
rows.model: Share of model first-birth flow in cells beginning at 30 or above.
rows.assessment: Threshold matches a model cell boundary. Period/population and support assumptions still require a declared target interpretation.

rows.weight_rationale: Recorded empirical bootstrap standard error under the retained estimator/sample
rows.label: Aggregate wealth / annual earnings
rows.data: National PSID 2003/2005: weighted total net worth of reference-person families 18-85 divided by weighted gross labor earnings for working-age families. Ratio of sums, not mean household ratio.
rows.model: Beginning net financial wealth plus owner housing value, divided by annualized gross model labor earnings. Four-year flows are annualized once and payroll tax is grossed up.
rows.assessment: Arithmetic and annualization are verified. Reconcile mortgage/net-worth components and stock versus income reference dates before treating this as an exact empirical counterpart.

rows.weight_rationale: Inherited synthetic five-percent target scale; not empirical SE
rows.label: Annual bequests / aggregate wealth
rows.data: Inherited external historical restriction. No in-repository microdata builder or empirical SE; this review verifies its stored value, not its primary-source derivation.
rows.model: Expected nonnegative estate flows at death, annualized once, divided by aggregate beginning wealth; terminal death is imposed.
rows.assessment: Verify the source definition and accept or revise the external restriction explicitly. Its 5% tolerance is synthetic, not estimated precision. No automatic dropping: preserve bequest-block identification.

rows.weight_rationale: Recorded empirical bootstrap standard error under the retained estimator/sample
rows.label: Old wealth/income p90 / median
rows.data: National PSID 2003/2005 reference persons 76-84, family income above $1000 and observed child history. Weighted 90th percentile of net-worth/family-income divided by its weighted median.
rows.model: Same quantile operation and explicit 76-84 cell overlap, but income is modeled pension plus configured transfer. The scorer unambiguously uses this observer, not the legacy label-age statistic.
rows.assessment: Family income contains components absent from the pension proxy. Income threshold, observed-history selection and wealth components need reconciliation. This is a substantive mapping issue, not an ambiguous active scorer.

rows.weight_rationale: Recorded empirical bootstrap standard error under the retained estimator/sample
rows.label: Mean occupied rooms, cap 9
rows.data: ACS 2005/2006, selected 42 MET 2013 metros, household heads 18-85 and the saved housing-validity filters. Weighted rooms capped at 9. Reproduced exactly.
rows.model: Current realized owner/renter rooms capped at 9 in every income-resolved state before aggregation. Fractional age exposure is implemented.
rows.assessment: Cap/order implementation is verified. Decide national versus 42 metros and define the represented housing sample. Saved national counterpart is 5.607886.

rows.weight_rationale: Recorded empirical bootstrap standard error under the retained estimator/sample
rows.label: Ownership, heads 30-55
rows.data: ACS 2005/2006 heads 30-55 in 42 metros, positive household weights and the specified occupied-unit/structure sample. Weighted ownership share; reproduced exactly.
rows.model: Current realized owner mass over total mass, with half of the 54-57 cell included. No whole-cell age-mask error.
rows.assessment: Within-cell age uniformity is explicit. Geography and ACS structure types need a model interpretation. Saved national counterpart is 67.6260%; switching geography does not cure low ownership.

rows.weight_rationale: Recorded empirical bootstrap standard error under the retained estimator/sample
rows.label: First-birth room response
rows.data: Weighted national PSID household-aligned event study: coefficient at +3 minus coefficient at -1, omitted -2; person/year effects, age/education controls and person clustering. Stored scalar and SE reproduce.
rows.model: Matched treated/control branches advanced one four-year period under stationary policies, with destination continuation births allowed; uncapped rooms. This implemented calculation is not the same regression/cohort weighting.
rows.assessment: Not a settled target. Reference support and demonstrated normalization sensitivity remain; author preferred a -2 empirical baseline. Completed binned diagnostic 0.426502 is a different sample/design and is not a replacement. Fix the empirical estimand and model counterpart together.

rows.weight_rationale: Recorded empirical bootstrap standard error under the retained estimator/sample
rows.label: Rooms: 3+ versus 1-2 resident children
rows.data: ACS heads 30-55 with youngest resident own child under 18; compare all resident-own-child counts 3+ versus 1-2, with rooms capped 9. Exact saved reproduction.
rows.model: Model current dependents 3+ versus 1-2, restricted to feasible count states; caps full-state rooms before aggregation.
rows.assessment: Resident own children can include adult children; current dependents with stochastic departure are not that exact grouping. Choose and justify the shared measurement.

rows.weight_rationale: Recorded empirical bootstrap standard error under the retained estimator/sample
rows.label: Recent-parent ownership gap
rows.data: ACS heads 30-55: ownership where oldest resident own child is under 4 minus ownership with no resident own children. Exact saved reproduction.
rows.model: Synchronized current births from previously empty-dependent homes minus current empty homes, including former parents. This is the active repaired observer.
rows.assessment: Not the obsolete lifetime-childless comparison. It remains an approximation to an interview stock defined by oldest child age. Sampling uncertainty alone does not measure this discrepancy. National counterpart 12.7608 pp is available.

Resolve child-group and wealth-income definitions; distinguish acceptable declared model approximations from required empirical remeasurement. Preserve identification if any row is changed.
Document working weights by purpose, freeze the complete source/target/observer fingerprint, verify the exact measurement loop, then reconsider the two-utility overnight search.
